question: Where was the FIH Men's Indoor Hockey World Cup 2018 organised?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Berlin, Germany.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The FIH Men's Indoor Hockey World Cup 2018 (the 5th edition) was held in Berlin, Germany, from 7 to 11 February 2018. (इंडोर हॉकी विश्व कप 2018 — बर्लिन, जर्मनी)

 

• Host nation Germany won the tournament, defeating Austria in the final.

 

• Indoor hockey is a variant of field hockey played on a smaller indoor court with modified rules, distinct from the outdoor Hockey World Cup.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The outdoor Men's Hockey World Cup is a separate, larger tournament; India hosted the 2018 edition of the outdoor Men's Hockey World Cup in Bhubaneswar, Odisha.

 

• The FIH (International Hockey Federation) is headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland.

 

NOTE

 

• Poznan, Poland (Option 2): Has hosted other indoor hockey events but not the 2018 Men's Indoor World Cup.

 

• Vienna, Austria (Option 3): Austria was the losing finalist in 2018, not the host.

 

• Leipzig, Germany (Option 4): A German city, but the 2018 tournament was held in Berlin, not Leipzig.

question: How many fundamental duties are provided in the Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 11.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Constitution originally listed 10 Fundamental Duties under Article 51A, added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee. (मूल कर्तव्य — अनुच्छेद 51A)

 

• An 11th Fundamental Duty — the duty of a parent/guardian to provide opportunities for education to their child/ward aged 6 to 14 years — was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002.

 

• Fundamental Duties are found in Part IVA of the Constitution and are inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR (Soviet Union).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, i.e., they cannot be directly enforced by courts, unlike Fundamental Rights.

 

• Part IVA (Article 51A) was added on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee (1976).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (12), Option 3 (14), Option 4 (17): These figures do not match the actual number of Fundamental Duties (11) listed under Article 51A.

question: In the context of India, tropical cyclones originate over the __________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bay of Bengal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the Indian context, tropical cyclones predominantly originate over the Bay of Bengal, which generates roughly four times as many cyclones as the Arabian Sea due to warmer sea-surface temperatures and inflow of fresh water from rivers. (उष्णकटिबंधीय चक्रवात — बंगाल की खाड़ी)

 

• These cyclones typically form between 8° and 20° N latitude over warm ocean waters (sea-surface temperature above 26–27°C) and derive energy from the latent heat of condensation.

 

• Cyclones forming in the Bay of Bengal mainly strike the eastern coast of India (Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, West Bengal) and Bangladesh/Myanmar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Arabian Sea also generates tropical cyclones, though fewer and generally less intense, affecting Gujarat, Maharashtra and the Oman/Pakistan coasts.

 

• The India Meteorological Department (IMD) is the Regional Specialised Meteorological Centre (RSMC) for cyclone warnings in the North Indian Ocean.

 

NOTE

 

• Arabian Sea (Option 1): Also part of the North Indian Ocean basin, but generates fewer cyclones than the Bay of Bengal.

 

• Pacific Ocean (Option 2): Storms there are called typhoons/hurricanes and do not directly form off India's coasts in this context.

 

• Mediterranean Sea (Option 4): Not relevant to Indian tropical cyclones; occasional 'medicanes' there are a different, unrelated phenomenon.

question: Which of the following UT/states have the highest density/km², according to census 2011?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Census 2011, Bihar recorded a population density of about 1,102 persons per km², the highest among all Indian states (as distinct from Union Territories). (बिहार — सर्वाधिक जनसंख्या घनत्व वाला राज्य)

 

• Bihar's high density is linked to its fertile Gangetic plains, which support intensive agriculture and dense rural settlement.

 

• Among the options given, Bihar is the state (as opposed to Union Territory) with the highest density recorded in Census 2011.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Among Union Territories, Delhi (~11,320/km²) has the highest density in the country, followed by Chandigarh (~9,252/km²) and Puducherry (~2,598/km²) — all denser than any state, but categorised separately from states.

 

• India's overall population density per Census 2011 was about 382 persons per km².

 

NOTE

 

• Pondicherry (Option 1): A Union Territory with a density (~2,598/km²) higher than Bihar's, but the question is understood, per the official key, as asking for the densest state.

 

• Chandigarh (Option 2): Also a Union Territory (~9,252/km²), denser than any state, but not the state-level answer intended here.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 3): UP's density (~828/km²) as per Census 2011 is lower than Bihar's.

question: Which college was established in Banaras in 1791?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hindu College, as per the officially released SSC CGL answer key for this question.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Banaras (Varanasi) has a long history as a centre of traditional and modern learning, home to institutions spanning several centuries. (बनारस — शिक्षा का प्राचीन केंद्र)

 

• The official answer key for this question marks Hindu College as the institution established at Banaras in 1791.

 

• Banaras is also home to the much later Banaras Hindu University (BHU), founded in 1916 by Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya, one of India's largest residential universities.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3, as per the official answer key.

 

Additional Information

 

• A well-documented institution founded at Banaras in 1791 by the British administrator Jonathan Duncan was the Sanskrit College (later Government Sanskrit College, and today Sampurnanand Sanskrit Vishwavidyalaya) — students and readers cross-referencing other sources for this question should be aware some references instead credit that institution for the 1791 founding date.

 

• Presidency College, Calcutta, was also originally established as Hindu College in 1817, a separate institution from Banaras.

 

NOTE

 

• Dayanand College (Option 1): Not linked to an 1791 founding at Banaras.

 

• Shivaji College (Option 2): Not linked to an 1791 founding at Banaras.

 

• Sanskrit College (Option 4): Historically documented as the institution founded at Banaras in 1791 by Jonathan Duncan; it is a close alternative to this question's official answer — see Additional Information above.

question: Which country is the leading producer of rice?
solution_text:
The correct answer is China.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• China is the world's leading producer of rice, followed by India as the second-largest producer. (चावल उत्पादन — चीन सर्वोच्च)

 

• Rice is a kharif crop requiring high temperature, high humidity, and abundant rainfall (or irrigation), making it the staple food crop of much of South and East Asia.

 

• India, though the world's second-largest producer, is the largest exporter of rice globally.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major rice-producing countries include Indonesia, Bangladesh, Vietnam and Thailand.

 

• In India, West Bengal is typically the largest rice-producing state.

 

NOTE

 

• Japan (Option 2): A significant rice consumer but not among the top global producers.

 

• India (Option 3): The second-largest producer of rice, after China.

 

• Egypt (Option 4): Produces rice but in far smaller quantities than China or India.

question: Who has been appointed as new director of AIIMS, New Delhi in September 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is M. Srinivas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr. M. Srinivas, then Dean of ESIC Medical College, Hyderabad, was appointed as the new Director of AIIMS, New Delhi, in September 2022. (एम्स निदेशक — डॉ. एम. श्रीनिवास)

 

• He succeeded Dr. Randeep Guleria, who had completed his extended tenure as AIIMS Delhi Director.

 

• Dr. M. Srinivas is a surgical oncologist by specialisation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• AIIMS New Delhi was established in 1956 and is India's premier autonomous public medical institution.

 

• AIIMS directors are selected through a formal Union Health Ministry selection process.

 

NOTE

 

• Raj Subramaniam (Option 1): CEO of FedEx, unrelated to AIIMS.

 

• Krishnan Ramanujam (Option 3): A corporate executive (Tata Consultancy Services), unrelated to AIIMS.

 

• Nitin Chugh (Option 4): A banking executive, unrelated to AIIMS.

question: The Winter Olympics - 2026 will be hosted by _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Italy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2026 Winter Olympics will be jointly hosted by Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo, Italy, making it the third Winter Olympics held in Italy (after Cortina 1956 and Turin 2006). (शीतकालीन ओलंपिक 2026 — इटली)

 

• This will be the first Winter Games shared between two host regions in Italy (Lombardy and Veneto).

 

• The official name is the XXV Olympic Winter Games (Milano Cortina 2026).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2022 Winter Olympics were held in Beijing, China — the first city to host both Summer (2008) and Winter Olympics.

 

• The 2030 Winter Olympics are scheduled to be held in the French Alps, France.

 

NOTE

 

• Russia (Option 1): Hosted the 2014 Winter Olympics (Sochi), not 2026.

 

• Canada (Option 2): Hosted the 2010 Winter Olympics (Vancouver), not 2026.

 

• France (Option 4): Will host the 2030 Winter Olympics, not 2026.

question: Whom among the following Indian classical musicians is an auditorium in Teheran, Iran named after?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ustad Bismillah Khan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An auditorium named 'Tahar Mosiquee Ustad Bismillah Khan' is situated in Tehran, Iran, honouring the legendary Indian shehnai maestro. (शहनाई वादक — उस्ताद बिस्मिल्लाह खान)

 

• Ustad Bismillah Khan (1916–2006) popularised the shehnai as a classical solo instrument and famously performed at the Red Fort on India's first Independence Day (15 August 1947).

 

• He was honoured with the Bharat Ratna in 2001, India's highest civilian award.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bismillah Khan hailed from Dumraon, Bihar, and spent much of his career in Varanasi, associated with the Vishwanath Temple.

 

• He was also awarded Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibhushan before receiving the Bharat Ratna.

 

NOTE

 

• Ustad Sultan Khan (Option 2): A renowned sarangi player, not associated with this Tehran auditorium.

 

• Ustad Zakir Hussain (Option 3): A world-renowned tabla player, not associated with this Tehran auditorium.

 

• Ustad Vilayat Khan (Option 4): A celebrated sitar player, not associated with this Tehran auditorium.

question: Which type of rock can be considered as a biological sedimentary rock?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Limestone.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Limestone is classified as a biological (organic) sedimentary rock because it is largely formed from the accumulated skeletal remains and shells of marine organisms such as corals, molluscs and foraminifera, composed mainly of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃). (चूना पत्थर — जैविक अवसादी शैल)

 

• Sedimentary rocks are broadly classified as clastic (from rock fragments), chemical (from precipitation of dissolved minerals), and biological/organic (from organic remains) — limestone (and coal) fall in the biological category.

 

• On metamorphosis, limestone transforms into marble.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Coal is another important biological/organic sedimentary rock, formed from compressed plant remains.

 

• Examples of chemical sedimentary rocks include rock salt and gypsum.

 

NOTE

 

• Bauxite (Option 1): A residual sedimentary rock (the chief ore of aluminium), formed by chemical weathering, not biological in origin.

 

• Marble (Option 2): A metamorphic rock, formed from the recrystallisation of limestone under heat and pressure.

 

• Granite (Option 3): An igneous rock, formed from the cooling and solidification of magma.

question: Who discovered three chemical elements: cerium, thorium and selenium, and devised the modern method by which one or two letters are used to symbolise elements?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jacob Berzelius.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Swedish chemist Jöns Jacob Berzelius discovered the elements cerium, thorium and selenium, and introduced the modern system of representing chemical elements by one or two-letter symbols (derived from their Latin names). (रासायनिक प्रतीक प्रणाली — जैकब बर्जीलियस)

 

• Berzelius is also credited with determining accurate atomic weights for many elements and coining terms such as 'catalysis' and 'isomerism'.

 

• He is often regarded as one of the founders of modern chemistry.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Prior to Berzelius, alchemical/pictorial symbols (as used by Dalton) were common for representing elements.

 

• Berzelius also made major contributions to analytical chemistry and the study of silicon.

 

NOTE

 

• Hennig Brand (Option 1): Discovered the element phosphorus in 1669, unrelated to this discovery.

 

• Niels Bohr (Option 2): Known for his model of the atom, not for the element symbol notation.

 

• John Dalton (Option 4): Proposed modern atomic theory and used circular symbols for elements, which Berzelius's letter-based system later replaced.

question: With respect to India's foreign trade, which year is referred to as the year of divide?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1991.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 1991 is referred to as the 'year of divide' in India's foreign trade policy, marking the launch of sweeping economic liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation (LPG) reforms under Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh and PM P. V. Narasimha Rao. (आर्थिक उदारीकरण — वर्ष 1991)

 

• The reforms followed a severe Balance of Payments crisis, and included de-licensing of industries, rupee devaluation, and opening up of trade and foreign investment.

 

• India's trade policy shifted from an inward-looking, protectionist regime to an export-oriented, liberalised regime after 1991.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The New Industrial Policy, 1991 abolished industrial licensing for most industries (except a short reserved list).

 

• India also joined institutions such as the WTO (1995) as part of this post-1991 trade liberalisation trajectory.

 

NOTE

 

• 2010 (Option 1), 1981 (Option 3), 1996 (Option 4): None of these years mark the landmark shift in India's trade policy; that distinction belongs uniquely to 1991.

question: The elections to the Panchayati Raj institutions are conducted by the ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is State election commission.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Elections to Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) and Urban Local Bodies are conducted by the State Election Commission (SEC), as provided under Article 243K of the Constitution. (राज्य निर्वाचन आयोग — पंचायती राज चुनाव)

 

• Each state has its own SEC, headed by a State Election Commissioner, appointed by the Governor, distinct from the Election Commission of India (which conducts Lok Sabha/state assembly/presidential/Vice-Presidential elections).

 

• This provision was introduced by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, which gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 73rd Amendment deals with rural local bodies (Panchayats); the 74th Amendment deals with urban local bodies (Municipalities), both conducted by the SEC.

 

• The Election Commission of India (ECI) is a separate constitutional body under Article 324.

 

NOTE

 

• Central election commission (Option 1): No such body exists by this name; the ECI conducts national/state elections, not panchayat elections.

 

• State government (Option 2): Does not directly conduct these elections; the independent SEC does.

 

• Central government (Option 4): Has no role in conducting Panchayati Raj elections.

question: Money multiplier can be expressed as ______.
option_1: Statutory liquidity ratio / Cash Reserve Ratio
option_3: Cash reserve ratio – Statutory liquidity ratio
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1/ Cash Reserve Ratio.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The money multiplier, in its simplified textbook form, is expressed as 1/CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio) — it measures how much the money supply expands for every unit increase in the monetary base, given a certain reserve requirement. (मुद्रा गुणक — 1/नकद आरक्षित अनुपात)

 

• A lower CRR means banks hold fewer reserves and can lend more, resulting in a higher money multiplier and greater credit/money creation in the economy.

 

• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) uses CRR as one of its key monetary policy tools to control money supply and inflation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• A more complete formula for the money multiplier also accounts for the currency-deposit ratio, but for basic/textbook purposes, 1/CRR is the standard expression.

 

• Other monetary policy tools of the RBI include Repo Rate, Reverse Repo Rate, Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) and Open Market Operations.

 

NOTE

 

• SLR/CRR (Option 1): Not the standard expression for the money multiplier.

 

• 1/SLR (Option 2): SLR relates to the ratio of liquid assets banks must maintain, not the basis for the money multiplier formula.

 

• CRR – SLR (Option 3): Not a recognised formula for the money multiplier.

question: Who among the following is supposed to compile both the Puranas and the Mahabharata?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sage Vyasa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sage Vyasa (Ved Vyasa/Krishna Dwaipayana) is traditionally credited with compiling both the eighteen Mahapuranas and the epic Mahabharata. (महर्षि वेदव्यास — पुराण एवं महाभारत रचयिता)

 

• He is also credited with the compilation/classification of the four Vedas, earning him the title 'Veda Vyasa' ('compiler of the Vedas').

 

• In the Mahabharata narrative, Vyasa is himself a character — the biological grandfather of the Pandavas and Kauravas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ramayana was composed by Sage Valmiki, often called the 'Adi Kavi' (first poet) in Sanskrit literature.

 

• The Puranas are traditionally counted as 18 Mahapuranas and numerous Upapuranas.

 

NOTE

 

• Sage Vasishtha (Option 1): A revered Vedic-era rishi and royal guru of the Ikshvaku dynasty, not credited with compiling the Puranas/Mahabharata.

 

• Sage Bharadwaja (Option 2): Another Vedic-era rishi, associated with hymns of the Rigveda, not this compilation.

 

• Sage Valmiki (Option 4): Credited with composing the Ramayana, not the Puranas/Mahabharata.

question: Sultan Mahmud came to India from which of the following city of Afghanistan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ghazni.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni ruled the Ghaznavid Empire from his capital at Ghazni, in present-day Afghanistan, and led a series of raids into the Indian subcontinent between 1000 and 1027 CE. (सुल्तान महमूद ग़ज़नवी — ग़ज़नी)

 

• His most notorious raid was on the Somnath Temple in Gujarat in 1025 CE, during which he plundered its wealth.

 

• Mahmud's court included the celebrated scholar Al-Biruni, who documented Indian society and science in his work *Kitab-ul-Hind*.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The later invader Muhammad of Ghor (whose successors founded the Delhi Sultanate) ruled from Ghor, a different Afghan region, distinct from Ghazni.

 

• Mahmud of Ghazni carried out a total of about 17 invasions into India.

 

NOTE

 

• Jalalabad (Option 2), Kabul (Option 3), Kandahar (Option 4): Other cities of Afghanistan, but Mahmud's base and title were tied to Ghazni, not these cities.

question: In which year did Langmuir reform the Lewis concept by abandoning the idea of a stable cubical arrangement of the octet and introducing the term 'covalent bond'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1919.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 1919, American chemist Irving Langmuir refined G. N. Lewis's octet theory by abandoning the idea of a static cubical arrangement of the octet and introduced the term 'covalent bond' to describe electron-pair sharing between atoms. (सहसंयोजक बंध शब्द — इरविंग लैंगम्यूर, 1919)

 

• Lewis had earlier (1916) proposed that atoms achieve stability by sharing electron pairs, initially visualised via a cubical atom model.

 

• Langmuir's refinement led to the modern Lewis-Langmuir theory of covalent bonding, foundational to the study of chemical bonding.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Irving Langmuir later won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1932 for his work in surface chemistry.

 

• G. N. Lewis proposed the Lewis dot structure for representing valence electrons, still used today.

 

NOTE

 

• 1915, 1921, 1917 (Options 2, 3, 4): None of these years mark Langmuir's introduction of the term 'covalent bond'; the correct year is 1919.

question: Jagoi and cholom are the two main divisions in which Classical dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manipuri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Manipuri classical dance, the two main stylistic divisions are Jagoi (the dance/movement component) and Cholom (the more vigorous, often martial, drum-dance component). (जागोई और चोलोम — मणिपुरी नृत्य)

 

• Manipuri dance is deeply rooted in Vaishnavite themes, especially the Radha-Krishna Raas Leela tradition, and is one of the eight classical dance forms of India recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.

 

• It originates from the state of Manipur in North-East India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Famous exponents of Manipuri dance include Guru Bipin Singh and the Jhaveri Sisters.

 

• Other classical dance forms of India include Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Odissi, Kuchipudi, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

 

NOTE

 

• Bharatanatyam (Option 1): Classical dance of Tamil Nadu, structured around adavus and margam, not Jagoi/Cholom.

 

• Odissi (Option 2): Classical dance of Odisha, characterised by the tribhangi posture, not Jagoi/Cholom.

 

• Mohiniyattam (Option 4): Classical dance of Kerala, a graceful solo lasya-style dance, not Jagoi/Cholom.

question: Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra, who was awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 2000, was an exponent of which of the following classical dances of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odissi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra (1926–2004) was a legendary exponent and one of the chief architects of modern Odissi classical dance, and was awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 2000. (केलुचरण महापात्र — ओडिसी नृत्य)

 

• He trained many celebrated dancers, including Sonal Mansingh, Sanjukta Panigrahi and Madhavi Mudgal, and was instrumental in reviving and codifying Odissi in the mid-20th century.

 

• Odissi originated in the temples of Odisha, particularly associated with the Jagannath Temple tradition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kelucharan Mohapatra earlier received the Padma Shri (1975) and Padma Bhushan (1988) before the Padma Vibhushan.

 

• Odissi is characterised by the distinctive Tribhangi (three-bend) posture and the Chowka and Tribhangi stances.

 

NOTE

 

• Kathakali (Option 1): Classical dance-drama of Kerala, not associated with Kelucharan Mohapatra.

 

• Kathak (Option 3): Classical dance of North India, associated with gurus like Birju Maharaj, not Kelucharan Mohapatra.

 

• Mohiniyattam (Option 4): Classical dance of Kerala, unrelated to Kelucharan Mohapatra.

question: How much purse money was given to a recipient of the Akademi Award in 2019?
solution_text:
The correct answer is ₹1 lakh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sahitya Akademi Award (India's National Academy of Letters award), commonly referred to as the 'Akademi Award', carried a purse of ₹1 lakh as of 2019, along with a citation and an engraved copper-plaque. (साहित्य अकादमी पुरस्कार — ₹1 लाख)

 

• The award recognises the most outstanding books of literary merit published in any of the languages officially recognised by the Sahitya Akademi, including English.

 

• The Sahitya Akademi was established in 1954 and is headquartered in New Delhi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sahitya Akademi also confers the Bhasha Samman and Translation Prizes for works in various Indian languages.

 

• Similar bodies for other art forms include the Sangeet Natak Akademi (performing arts) and Lalit Kala Akademi (visual arts).

 

NOTE

 

• ₹4 lakh, ₹2 lakh, ₹3 lakh (Options 2, 3, 4): These amounts do not correspond to the Sahitya Akademi Award's purse money as of 2019, which was ₹1 lakh.

question: Who has been appointed as a brand ambassador of Punyakoti Dattu Yojana?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kichcha Sudeep.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kannada film actor Kichcha Sudeep was appointed as the brand ambassador of the Punyakoti Dattu Yojana, a Karnataka government scheme for the adoption/fostering of cattle (especially orphaned calves and stray cattle). (पुण्यकोटि दत्तु योजना — कर्नाटक)

 

• The scheme is named after the mythical cow Punyakoti, referenced in a well-known Kannada folk tale symbolising truthfulness and sacrifice.

 

• The scheme allows citizens to symbolically 'adopt' cattle housed in government Gosalas (cow shelters) by paying a nominal maintenance amount.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Punyakoti Dattu Yojana falls under the Karnataka Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Services Department.

 

• Kichcha Sudeep is also a well-known TV host, notably of the Kannada version of *Bigg Boss*.

 

NOTE

 

• Rana Daggubati (Option 1): A Telugu film actor, not associated with this scheme.

 

• Mahesh Babu (Option 3): A Telugu film actor, not associated with this scheme.

 

• Sonu Sood (Option 4): An actor known for humanitarian/relief work, not associated with this specific scheme.

question: The second volume of the Akbar Nama recorded the _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Events of Akbar's reign.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Akbar Nama, written by Abul Fazl (a courtier of Emperor Akbar), is divided into three volumes; the second volume records the events of Akbar's reign, covering the history up to his 46th regnal year. (अकबरनामा — दूसरा खंड, अकबर के शासनकाल की घटनाएँ)

 

• The first volume covers the history of Akbar's ancestors — Timur's line, Babur and Humayun, and the Sur Sultans.

 

• The third volume is the celebrated Ain-i-Akbari, an administrative gazetteer detailing Akbar's governance, revenue and household regulations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Abul Fazl was assassinated in 1602 on the orders of Prince Salim (later Jahangir), reportedly leaving the Akbar Nama's final portion incomplete.

 

• The Akbar Nama is one of the most important primary sources for the political and administrative history of Akbar's reign.

 

NOTE

 

• Akbar's ancestors (Option 1): This is the subject of the first volume, not the second.

 

• Akbar's administration (Option 2): Administrative details are chiefly covered in the third volume (Ain-i-Akbari).

 

• Akbar's battles (Option 4): Battles are only one part of the broader narrative of events covered in the second volume; the volume's defining subject is the events of the reign as a whole, not battles alone.

question: Which of the following is a local wind?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Loo.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Loo is a strong, hot and dry local wind that blows during the day across the Indo-Gangetic Plains of North India in the summer months (April to June), often causing heatstroke. (लू — स्थानीय पवन)

 

• Local winds are caused by local temperature and pressure differences over a small area, unlike planetary winds (Westerlies, Easterlies) or seasonal winds (Monsoon), which operate on a much larger, global/regional scale.

 

• Loo typically blows from the west or north-west in the afternoon, and is a well-known feature of the pre-monsoon season in north-western and central India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other examples of local winds include the Mango Shower and Blossom Shower (Kerala) and Chinook/Foehn winds (mountain regions).

 

• The Monsoon is a seasonal wind caused by differential heating of land and sea on a sub-continental scale.

 

NOTE

 

• Westerlies (Option 2): Permanent/planetary winds blowing from the sub-tropical high to the sub-polar low, in both hemispheres.

 

• Monsoon (Option 3): A large-scale seasonal wind system affecting the Indian subcontinent, not a local wind.

 

• Easterlies (Option 4): Permanent/planetary winds, including the Trade Winds and Polar Easterlies, blowing over large latitudinal belts, not a local wind.

question:
Match Column-A with Column-B.

Column-A (Organelle) | Column-B (Function)

i. Mitochondria | a. Protein synthesis

ii. Ribosomes | b. Regulation of activity of a cell

iii. Nucleus | c. Digestive system of a cell

iv. Lysosomes | d. Energy generation
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-d, ii-a, iii-b, iv-c.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mitochondria (i) are the 'powerhouse of the cell', responsible for energy generation (d) through aerobic respiration and ATP synthesis. (माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया — कोशिका का पावर हाउस)

 

• Ribosomes (ii) are the site of protein synthesis (a), translating mRNA into polypeptide chains; they may be free in the cytoplasm or bound to the endoplasmic reticulum.

 

• The Nucleus (iii) contains the cell's genetic material (DNA) and acts as the control/regulatory centre of cell activities (b), directing metabolism, growth and reproduction.

 

• Lysosomes (iv), often called the 'suicide bags' of the cell, contain hydrolytic enzymes and function as the digestive system of the cell (c), breaking down waste materials, worn-out organelles and foreign particles.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mitochondria have their own circular DNA and ribosomes, supporting the endosymbiotic theory of their origin.

 

• The endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi apparatus work together with ribosomes and lysosomes in protein synthesis, processing and packaging.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (i-c, ii-a, iii-d, iv-c): Incorrectly assigns mitochondria the digestive function and the nucleus the energy-generation function, and repeats 'c' for lysosomes.

 

• Option 2 (i-b, ii-a, iii-c, iv-d): Incorrectly assigns mitochondria the regulatory function and lysosomes the energy-generation function.

 

• Option 3 (i-a, ii-b, iii-c, iv-d): Incorrectly assigns mitochondria the protein-synthesis function and ribosomes the regulatory function.

question: Which state government has launched the novel 'Chief Minister's Breakfast Scheme' in September 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Tamil Nadu government, under Chief Minister M. K. Stalin, launched the 'Chief Minister's Breakfast Scheme' in September 2022, initially in select government schools in Chennai, to provide free nutritious breakfast to primary school children. (मुख्यमंत्री नाश्ता योजना — तमिलनाडु)

 

• The scheme aims to improve child nutrition, boost school attendance, and reduce classroom fatigue among young students.

 

• It was later expanded to cover many more government and government-aided schools across Tamil Nadu.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tamil Nadu has a long-standing history of school nutrition programmes, dating back to the Nutritious Meal Programme launched by then Chief Minister M. G. Ramachandran in 1982.

 

• The scheme has been widely cited as a model for improving learning outcomes through better child nutrition.

 

NOTE

 

• Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Himachal Pradesh (Options 1, 3, 4): These states did not launch this particular scheme in September 2022; it is specific to Tamil Nadu.
